title: Ice cream, vanilla, with additional ingredients

content.title: About
content.content: Vanilla ice cream is a classic dessert made from milk, cream, sugar and natural vanilla flavoring. In this version additional ingredients (such as nuts, chocolate chips, berries) are mixed into the base, enriching both taste and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vanilla is the most expensive spice in the world; its flavor comes from the seeds of the orchid Vanilla planifolia.
The first vanilla‑flavoured ice cream appeared in Europe in the 17th century.
Adding extra ingredients allows for more than 400 flavor variations, making ice cream a highly versatile dessert.
Vanilla ice cream is often used in culinary shows for “soft‑serve” effects because it molds easily.
Traditionally ice cream was served as a soft scoop, but modern techniques create rolls, sandwiches, and even milk‑shake‑style desserts.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Dairy components provide calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cream and milk contain vitamin B12 and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Vanilla antioxidants
items.content: Vanilla contains vanillin, an antioxidant that helps combat free radicals.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The fat and sugar content offers a rapid source of energy when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Mood‑boosting effect
items.content: Sweet taste and creamy texture can improve mood by triggering endorphin release.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dairy ingredients may cause discomfort for people lacking lactase.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption can contribute to weight gain and elevated blood glucose.

items.title: Allergy to nuts or other add‑ins
items.content: If nuts, chocolate, or berries are included, allergic reactions are possible.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Ice cream is rich in fats and calories, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ice cream can be enjoyed with a spoon, as an ice‑cream sandwich, blended into smoothies, or used as a base for dessert sauces. Sprinkle extra ingredients (nuts, fruit, chocolate) just before serving to keep them crunchy.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ice cream in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, use within 1–2 weeks to prevent ice crystal formation and flavor loss. Do not leave ice cream at room temperature for more than 30 minutes.
